description: TAG‑195, also known as Golden Chickens or Venom Spider, operates as a financially motivated malware-as-a-service (MaaS) provider that has released a modular suite of backdoors including TinyEgg, ChonkyChicken, and ChromEggscalator. The group uses deceptive ClickFix fake security pages for initial access, establishes persistence via registry run keys, and communicates over WebSocket C2 channels while employing obfuscation to evade detection. Its campaigns target a wide swath of industries—government, defense, finance, energy, telecommunications, and many others—across dozens of countries.
goals: TAG‑195’s primary objective is financial gain, achieved by delivering customized backdoors to a wide customer base through its MaaS model. The actor targets high-value sectors—including government, defense, critical infrastructure, finance, energy, telecommunications, healthcare, and maritime—across both Western and Eastern markets (CN, RU, US, UK, JP, etc.). By focusing on industries that frequently use shared web browsers and legacy systems, TAG‑195 maximizes the potential for credential theft while minimizing development overhead. The broad geographic reach indicates a deliberate strategy of risk dispersion and opportunistic targeting rather than narrow geopolitical objectives.
